claims: Six conditional mathematical UNSAT counterexample checks, satisfiable premises, one SAT old-boundary witness. No Kotlin/AtomicFile/Android/cryptographic proof. Linux alias witness is separately labeled.

results.model: one restore is representable and preserves reserve
results.hypotheses: Existing archived ID; exact update (r,a)->(r+1,a-1). No failed IO, external writer, rollback or miscount.

(declare-fun archived () Int)
(assert
 (>= revision 0))
(assert
 (>= archived 0))
(assert
 (<= archived 128))
(assert
 (let ((?x13 (+ revision archived)))
 (<= ?x13 9223372036854775807)))
(assert
 (>= archived 1))
(assert
 (or (> (+ revision 1) 9223372036854775807) (> (+ (+ revision 1) (- archived 1)) 9223372036854775807) (< (- archived 1) 0)))
(check-sat)

old_boundary.scope: Old archive admission can succeed without enough revision space to restore. Mathematical witness; separately compiled Kotlin witness is retained separately.

unlink_alias.scope: Actual Linux IO: a preexisting writable alias defeats immutability despite unlink and read-only reader. Production closes its writer and assumes a trusted private owner; this is NOT a reproduced Android exploit.
